The biggest skill advantage is in bug documentation format: with-skill consistently uses skipped tests with BUG suffix per the workflow, while baseline agents use ad-hoc approaches (t.Logf, comments, summary-only)
TypeScript eval shows no assertion difference (both score 100%) — the baseline was surprisingly strong on this eval, finding all the same bugs. This eval may not discriminate well.
Python baseline missed the split_payment(0) zero-division test entirely — a key bug the skill's checklist catches
Go baseline missed WrapText zero-width test — the skill's boundary condition checklist prompted testing this edge case
With-skill runs used significantly more tokens (mean 46K vs 27K) and time (mean 228s vs 151s), reflecting the phased workflow overhead
Note: Python with-skill timing (20s) is misleadingly low because the subagent was blocked on permissions and tests were run manually; actual workflow time was longer
